title: Agentic Memory: Learning Unified Long-Term and Short-Term Memory Management for Large Language Model Agents
problem_statement: Existing agent memory systems treat LTM and STM as independent components optimized separately, leading to fragmented memory construction and suboptimal long-horizon performance. Unified joint management of both memory types through a learnable policy remains unexplored.
key_ideas: Unified tool-based interface for both LTM (ADD, UPDATE, DELETE) and STM (RETRIEVE, SUMMARY, FILTER) management integrated directly into the agent's policy
Three-stage progressive RL strategy: Stage 1 (LTM construction from context), Stage 2 (STM control under distractors with context reset), Stage 3 (integrated reasoning with both memory types)
Step-wise GRPO: terminal trajectory reward broadcast uniformly to all timesteps for long-range credit assignment across heterogeneous memory operations

Composite reward covering task completion (Rtask), context management (Rcontext = compression + preventive + preservation), and memory quality (Rmemory = storage quality + maintenance + semantic relevance)
RL training on HotpotQA only; zero-shot generalization to 4 additional diverse long-horizon benchmarks
method_summary: AgeMem integrates 6 memory tools into the LLM agent's action space. Training uses a three-stage progressive RL curriculum: Stage 1 exposes casual context for LTM construction, Stage 2 resets context and injects distractors to train STM filtering, Stage 3 presents the full task requiring coordinated retrieval and reasoning. K=8 independent rollouts per task; group-normalized terminal rewards are broadcast to all timesteps (step-wise GRPO). The composite reward uses uniform 1/3 weighting across task, context, and memory components. Trained only on HotpotQA; evaluated on ALFWorld, SciWorld, PDDL, BabyAI, and HotpotQA.
contributions: AgeMem: first unified framework jointly managing LTM and STM via learnable tool-based policy
Three-stage progressive RL strategy that curriculum-trains memory acquisition, context filtering, and integrated coordination
Step-wise GRPO for long-range credit assignment across heterogeneous memory operations
Composite reward design covering task performance, context compression, and memory quality
Demonstration that unified memory management with RL improves both task performance AND memory quality simultaneously
limitations_acknowledged: Fixed set of memory tools limits fine-grained control
Evaluated on limited benchmark selection relative to real-world task diversity
limitations_observed: RL training only on HotpotQA may not learn optimal memory behaviors for spatial/planning tasks
No analysis of memory content evolution across many tasks in deployment
No ablation on removing individual training stages
Memory Quality metric only available for HotpotQA where ground-truth facts exist
Reward weights and KL coefficient not ablated
relevance_to_thesis: Most technically sophisticated memory controller in thesis reading list. The 6-tool action space (ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/RETRIEVE/SUMMARY/FILTER) is a complete implementable design. Three-stage progressive RL is a curriculum for teaching memory management from task-level feedback — directly relevant to educability. Cross-benchmark generalization from HotpotQA training demonstrates transfer of learned memory policies. Step-wise GRPO credit assignment mechanism is applicable to any thesis experiment involving RL-trained memory behaviors.
gaps_and_questions: Can the RL-trained memory policy transfer to different model backbones?
What happens with multi-domain RL training beyond HotpotQA?
Can memory quality reward serve as an independent teaching signal for knowledge transfer?
Would simpler reward designs achieve comparable results?
How does memory content evolve across extended deployment with diverse tasks?
poc_ideas: Implement AgeMem 3-stage progressive RL as thesis training curriculum for memory controller
Test whether step-wise GRPO credit assignment improves memory learning vs. only rewarding final task outcomes
Compare AgeMem (RL-based) vs. MemP/ReMe (prompt-based) on same benchmark to understand training cost vs. performance tradeoffs
Investigate whether AgeMem composite reward components serve as teaching signals in knowledge distillation from teacher to student agent
